small_guidance:
- Correctness failed with avg diff ~3e-4, max ~1.7e-3 — likely TF32 precision on a K=8192 reduction. Set `allow_tf32=False` in `tl.dot` (or cast inputs explicitly) and re-check; the loose 5e-2 tolerance should pass but the harness reports mismatch, so verify against fp32 reference exactly.
- After fixing precision, prune autotune configs to the top performers for M=N=K=8192 (BLOCK_M=128,BLOCK_N=256,BLOCK_K=32-64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) to cut autotune overhead.
- Since M, N, K are all multiples of 128, drop masking on the K loop (use a fast inner loop without `k_remaining` masks) and only mask the boundary; this reduces predicate overhead.
large_guidance:
- Keep the fused GEMM+sigmoid+scale+residual structure — it is the right design. The rewrite should focus on a split-K or stream-K variant since K=8192 is large and a single program reducing all of K may underutilize SMs; alternatively a persistent kernel with one program per SM looping over output tiles.
- Store weight in [N, K] layout with N-major access so each program loads a contiguous N-tile slab, or stick with [K,N] but use `tl.dot` with explicit fp32 accumulation and an fp32 weight cache to avoid TF32 drift.
- Consider an epilogue-fused approach where two GEMM tiles are pipelined per program (double-buffered K loop with `num_stages=4`) to hide global loads behind compute.
